xrefdescription.para: LTB-01a: Adapter with matching checksum → verifyChecksum returns true.
LTB-01b: Full checkAdapter pipeline with correct checksum → is_valid.
LTB-02a: verifyChecksum with tampered data → returns false.
LTB-02b: checkAdapter with mismatched checksum in metadata → is_valid=false.
LTB-02c: Empty adapter data with non-empty checksum → rejected.
LTB-03a: STRICT trust registry + unknown signer → adapter rejected.

detaileddescription.para: Governance requirement: an adapter from an unrecognised signer must NOT be loaded under a strict trust policy.

xrefdescription.para: LTB-03b: LENIENT trust registry + unknown signer → loaded with warning.

detaileddescription.para: Documented behaviour: lenient policy accepts unknown signers but MUST emit a warning so operators can detect and remediate.
Governance note: lenient mode must only be used in development environments. Production deployments must use STRICT mode (see ROADMAP.md §LoRA Trust).

xrefdescription.para: LTB-03c: Known signer under STRICT policy → no warning, accepted.

detaileddescription.para: Confirms the positive path: registered signers load without warnings under the strict policy.

xrefdescription.para: LTB-03d: End-to-end load simulation — unknown signer under strict policy prevents the adapter from reaching checkAdapter.

detaileddescription.para:
This test models the complete trust chain:
Check signer trust (registry gate).
Only proceed to checksum/checkAdapter when signer is trusted.

Acceptance criteria: LTB-01 Adapter with correct checksum → AdapterConsistencyChecker accepts the adapter (is_valid == true). LTB-02 Adapter with tampered data (wrong checksum) → checker rejects it (is_valid == false). LTB-03 Adapter from an unknown signer_id without a registered verifier → the loading behaviour is clearly defined: the adapter is rejected when the trust policy is strict, or accepted-with-warning when lenient. Both outcomes are explicitly documented; no silent pass.
All infrastructure is fully in-process; no real model files are required. The AdapterConsistencyChecker is used directly; signer_id enforcement is layered via a thin in-test trust registry.
